strongest_bounded_proposition: Slavery and slave export were materially present in the Merina/Imerina political economy around 1800, but specialist scholarship rejects treating slavery alone as the later imperial economy's single organising labour principle.
strongest_unsupported_proposition: Do not flatten slavery and fanompoana into one coerced-labour category or infer that all Merina production depended on slaves.
territorial_practice_summary: Slaveholding and slave labour are supported around 1800; later fanompoana formed a distinct crown-labour institution.
legal_state_summary: Crown/state labour obligations and slavery must remain separate.
external_network_summary: Slave exports were economically important around 1800 and later restricted by British-Merina agreements.
terminology_category_qualification: Slavery and fanompoana are distinct although both involve coercive dependency.
temporal_scope_precision: Sources directly cover Imerina from 1775/1790 through the nineteenth century and the 1800 anchor.
inference_extent: Bounded Merina claim; no island-wide prevalence inference.
language_access_limitations: English-accessible research packet only; non-English and non-digitized scholarship was not exhaustively searched.
